params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The young man at the desk, seen from behind, sits still for a beat with both hands resting on the keyboard, then leans in towards the middle monitor and types in one quick rattling burst, both hands bouncing across the keys, his shoulders bobbing with them. He stops dead, tips his head a little to one side as he reads the screen, then types a second, shorter burst, and taps one last key with one firm finger and a small flick of the wrist. He sits back in the chair, both hands settling on the edge of the desk, and holds still.

The back of his head, his short blonde hair and his navy T-shirt are the same in every frame. The chair stays at the desk in the same spot in every frame. The three monitors stay the same three dark screens with the same faint lines of code in every frame, and the desk, the cork board, the shelf of binders and the whiteboard stay the same drawings in every frame. The small brass bell hangs still on its bracket and the fat striped confetti cannon stands quiet on its tripod in the same spots in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
